title: feat(plugin-approvals): engine-written display labels for the approval lists (step, flow, waiting on, record pointer, acted-as)
body:
Fixes #23889
Clause-②: yes (widening)

## What this does

The Approvals Requests and Action History lists are generic list views. They show stored columns and nothing else, so admins read node ids, `flow:` api names, slot addresses and raw user ids. The approval engine (`ApprovalService`) now writes display columns beside the machine ones, and the list views show them. A list never re-derives a label from flow metadata and never resolves an approver address itself. Nothing is removed or renamed.

| object | new column | written when | shown in |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `sys_approval_request` | `process_label` (the flow's label) | open | every list view, in place of `process_name` |
| `sys_approval_request` | `current_step_label` (the Approval node's label) | open | `all_requests`, `my_pending`, `submitted_by_me`, in place of `current_step` |
| `sys_approval_request` | `pending_approver_labels` ("Waiting On") | every write that sets `pending_approvers` (open, partial tally, reassign, SLA reassign); cleared with it on every terminal write | `all_requests`, `my_pending` |
| `sys_approval_action` | `step_label` | each action, copied from the request | `recent`, `all_actions`, `by_actor`, in place of `step_name` |
| `sys_approval_action` | `object_name` + `record_id` (`referenceVia: 'object_name'`) | each action, copied from the request | `recent`, `all_actions` |
| `sys_approval_action` | `acted_as_label` | each action, when `acted_as` is set | `recent`, `all_actions`, in place of `acted_as` |

- **Labels.** The flow engine already hands the flow and node labels to `openNodeRequest` (`$flowLabel` and `node.label`, both required by the spec). So `service-automation` needed no change, and `engine.ts` is untouched. The labels used to live only in `node_config_json` (`__flowLabel` / `__nodeLabel`), which the inbox door read and a list view cannot. The inbox door's `process_label` / `step_label` now read the columns first, with the old fallbacks for earlier rows, so what the inbox serves is unchanged.
- **Slot labels** (`pending_approver_labels`, `acted_as_label`). A slot that names a person (a user id, or an email an account carries) gets the account's name from `resolveUserNames`. That is the resolver the approvals door already uses for `pending_approver_names` and the timeline's names. Any other slot (`position:` / `team:` literals) shows as its stored address, which is what the inbox does today.
- **One row builder for the decision log.** `actionRow(request, action)` adds the four copied columns. All 15 `sys_approval_action` inserts call it and each keeps its own `engine.insert(..., { context: SYSTEM_CTX })`, so the tenant-audit census still certifies every write call site. A first cut funnelled them through one writer, and that census correctly went red. Patch round 1's boot backfill adds two SYSTEM-context `engine.update` sites, so the census now certifies 229: regenerated with `node scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs --write`, with the census page's six gate-held figures set to the census's own values.

## Premise check (the card's measured table, re-read on `origin/main` `6d1660dc3b`)

| row | holds? |
|:--|:--|
| request list views show `current_step` (node id) | holds: all three caller-facing views listed `current_step` |
| `process_name` = `flow:NAME` | holds: `openNodeRequest` writes `flow:` plus the flow name |
| nothing says whom a pending request waits on; `pending_approvers` is a CSV of slot addresses | holds |
| action `request_id` displays `display_title` = `process_name · record_id` | holds; unchanged here. The new record pointer is what names the record |
| `acted_as` is a raw slot address | holds (the column holds the slot's stored spelling, by design, ADR-0118 D1) |
| `step_name` is the node id | holds |
| "the same resolver decide-time re-resolution uses (user name, position label, team label)" | **does not hold as worded.** Decisions are judged against the slate snapshotted at open, not re-resolved, and no resolver in the package produces position or team labels. The display resolver that exists is `resolveUserNames`, and that is the one used. Position and team labels are an open question in the report |
| a "step advance" write | there is none inside a request: each Approval node opens its own request (`current_step_index` is always 0), so the step label is written once, at open |

## Read security: the rule applied

Every new value on a row is either a column of the request that the row's readers already read, or a name the approvals door already serves those same readers for that same request, from the same resolver under the same system read.

- The generic data door serves `sys_approval_request` only to the callers the approvals door would (`request-read-gate.ts`, pinned by `request-read-gate.integration.test.ts`), and serves `sys_approval_action` only where its request is visible (`bindRequestChildReadGates`, pinned by `request-child-read-gate.integration.test.ts`). The action's gate is keyed on `request_id` only, so the new `object_name` / `record_id` columns add no new targeting: a read pinned on them is untargeted, which means narrower.
- Names: `enrichRows` already serves `pending_approver_names` (and `listActions` the timeline's names) from `resolveUserNames` under `SYSTEM_CTX` to exactly those readers. Pin (e) asserts that every label in `pending_approver_labels` is a name the approvals door serves the same reader for the same request, or the slot's own address.
- Record pointer: a pair of ids the reader already reads on the parent request. Nothing here serves a target-record title. The console's pointer cell (objectstack-ai/objectui#12658) titles the record through its own read as the reader, which the target's gates decide (the #23618 / #23637 discipline applies on that path, not here).
- A stored snapshot cannot be narrowed per reader. That is acceptable only because the names it holds are not narrowed per reader on the approvals door either. If that door ever narrows names by `sys_user` field-level security, these columns must follow. That is noted as an open question.

## Rows written before this change

A boot-time pass fills them, built over patch rounds 1–3 (REWORKs `6220012954`, `6221769417` and `6222977426`; addenda `6221489557`, `6222614009` and `6223588562`). `backfillApprovalDisplayLabels` (`src/display-label-backfill.ts`) runs on `kernel:ready`, after the action-slot repair: a keyset walk in pages of 500, one `sys_user` name read per page. A failure is logged at `warn`, and the next boot retries.
- **It keeps each row's `updated_at`.** Every fill write, and every write of the action-slot repair, runs under `{ isSystem: true, preserveAudit: true }` and passes the stored stamp back (`keptStamp`), so the lists that sort on `updated_at` keep their order. A row with no stored `updated_at` takes the write's instant: no update can keep it null.
- **It never lands a slate or a stamp older than the row.** Each request is re-read by id immediately before its write. The write names only the columns still null on that re-read row and passes back the re-read stamp. The waiting-on is written only while the row is still pending on the slate its names were read for. The one engine call between the re-read and the write is the remaining window, the same standard as `plugin-audit`'s comment-parent-pair backfill. The action passes write from their page read, because no live writer updates an action row.
- **Where `plugin-audit` is composed,** the first boot writes one system entry in the audit log and one in the record's activity timeline for each row it fills.
- **Requests:** `process_label` / `current_step_label` come from the one shared chain, `requestDisplayLabels` (`src/display-labels.ts`): the column, else `__flowLabel` / `__nodeLabel`, else the humanized machine name. The inbox door, the open write and `actionRow` all read the same chain, so no door can disagree with another. Pending rows get `pending_approver_labels` through `slateLabels`.
- **Actions:** `step_label` / `object_name` / `record_id` are copied from the parent request, and `acted_as_label` comes through `slotLabels(acted_as)`. `backfillActionSlots` now writes `acted_as_label` beside every `acted_as` it sets.
- **One boot fills every pre-change row, terminal ones included. A second boot writes nothing** (pins a–c in `display-label-backfill.integration.test.ts`).
- **A failed name read stores `null` for a person slot, never its address.** It warns once, and the next boot fills it. An empty authored label falls through to the humanized machine name at open.

## Tests

New `src/approval-list-display-labels.integration.test.ts`: the real `ApprovalService` on a real `ObjectQL` over `SqlDriver` (better-sqlite3, in-memory, real DDL):

- (a) open writes both labels and the waiting-on column, and the submit action carries the step label and pointer;
- (b) a partial tally rewrites the waiting-on column, each decision labels its slot (user id, then email, then position address), and the finalizing decision clears the column;
- (c) reassign and the SLA sweep's reassign rewrite it;
- (d) an action on a pre-change row copies the step label from the config snapshot;
- (e) read discipline;
- (f) the list-view declaration: display columns in place of the machine ones, every column a declared field, and `record_id` declaring `referenceVia: 'object_name'`.

At `c90771037` (round 0). The later readings are in the addenda: round 1 at `b74901ee3` (`6221489557`: 1,100 / 1,100 tests, 97 / 97 derived gates exit 0), round 2 at `f8efc941a` (`6222614009`: 1,102 / 1,102) and round 3 at `fbd7b4d3b` (`6223588562`: 1,103 / 1,103, 97 / 97 derived gates exit 0):

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: **80 files / 1094 tests passed**.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-approvals typecheck`: exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK, no new debt).
- `node scripts/check-i18n-bundles.mjs --filter=approvals`: in sync. The bundles were regenerated with `--write`, and zh-CN / ja-JP / es-ES values were written for the seven new keys.

**Ablations** (`scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, each restore proven blob == HEAD `55ada4ce937a` with `git diff HEAD` empty; green control 6/6 first):

| mutation | result |
|:--|:--|
| `slateLabels` returns null | red, 4 of 6 (a, b, c, e) |
| `actionRow` drops `object_name` | red, 4 of 6 (a, b, c, d) |
| `actionRow` drops `step_label` | red, 4 of 6 (a, b, c, d) |
| open writes no `current_step_label` | red, 1 of 6 (a). Actions then still label from the config snapshot, as designed |
| `acted_as_label` = raw `acted_as` | red, 2 of 6 (b, d) |

A first pass of these five came back red because `packages/spec/dist` went missing mid-run while a concurrent gate rebuilt it (each run said "no tests"). Those readings were discarded and the whole set was re-run on a stable tree.

## Gates

`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` at `c90771037` derives 67 commands. All were run, each exit captured before any pipe, and **all 67 exit 0**. `--ran` reconciliation: "67 derived, 67 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN" (a derived zero: every line carries its exit code). Two prerequisites were cleared before that run: the shallow clone was deepened to the commit `check-plugin-teardown-shape --self-test`'s fixture pins, and the dist trees `check:dual-build-cjs-loads` reads were built. CI families are read from this PR's check-runs.

## Acceptance notes

- `highlightFields` and `titleFormat` / `display_title` on both objects are unchanged. The request's record title still reads `flow:NAME · RECORD_ID` wherever it is drawn, for example in the action list's `request_id` cell. Switching it to `process_label` needs a null guard for earlier rows, and it touches `sys-approval-display-title.test.ts`'s pairing, so it is left for the console half (objectstack-ai/objectui#12608) to ask for.
- `sys-approval-request.page.ts` (PR #23837) and `packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts` (PR #23954) are untouched, as claimed. No `packages/spec` change: `ApprovalRequestRow` / `ApprovalActionRow` do not gain the new columns. They are served on the generic data door, which is what the lists read.
- No dogfood pin: the write path is pinned on a real engine. A real-boot console reading of the lists is NOT MEASURED in this PR.
